visual_review.flat_fields: black, blue/cyan, green, orange, white and yellow. Perceptual hash collision risk must not imply exact pixel identity.
visual_review.method: Pillow RGB thumbnails without color normalization, five source files per contact sheet; all20 inspected. Not a full-resolution artifact or colorimetric qualification.

findings: Wrapper imports Data.PHash, does not implement perceptual hashing locally. README requires unpinned external native phash and Haskell package; no build manifest or lock.

pairs enumerates whole Cartesian product and filters lexical a<=b and a/=b; O(n squared) pair generation and string comparisons, no index, cap or cancellation. Equal paths excluded but repeated inputs can emit repeated pairs. Source only, no Haskell execution.

readImg computes both image hashes for each pair, not once per image; n unique names produce n(n-1) imageHash calls vs n with memoization, excluding runtime errors. Source-derived call count, not measured speedup.
Default main only selects cat00/cat01/cat02, three unordered pairs and six imageHash calls. Other17 images exist but are not run by default; alternate sets are commented.

main returns sequence of result tuples without explicit printing, serialization, thresholds or assertions. compareHash/error strings are lazily constructed and not necessarily forced by IO result consumer. No executable-output or distance claim made.
compareHash handles Nothing with an error string, distinct from distance0; no decode-error identity alias in shown wrapper.
No expected distances, known-positive/negative table, recall/precision, runtime benchmark or test runner exists. Images illustrate cases rather than prove them.
MIT2015 Vladimir Alekseichenko wholly read; no separate image attribution/provenance contract in README or files. Do not copy external photos into project tests.

runtime.reason: No GHC/cabal on PATH; native pHash/ASAN explicitly deferred. No substitute Python hash presented as upstream result.

adoption: No code copied or production changes. Visual cases support separate candidate-vs-exact identity validation; no universal accuracy claim.
